title: Kitchen Food Safety
summary: The kitchen side of food safety: fridge and freezer temperatures, the 2-hour rule, three safe ways to thaw, how long leftovers keep, and using a food thermometer. The cooking temperatures are in the Food Safety Basics guide.

p: The site’s [Food Safety Basics](/meal-prep/guides/food-safety/) guide has the safe cooking temperatures for meat, poultry, fish and leftovers, and the four steps: clean, separate, cook, chill. This page adds the kitchen habits that go with them.

list: Keep the refrigerator at **40°F or below** and the freezer at **0°F or below**.
Put an appliance thermometer in each. The built-in dial shows a setting, not the temperature.

p: Refrigerate perishable food within **2 hours** of cooking or taking it out of the fridge, or within **1 hour** when it is above 90°F, like at a summer picnic. Throw out perishable food that has sat out longer.
Big pots of soup or chili cool slowly. Divide them into shallow containers, and cut large roasts into smaller pieces, so they chill fast.

rows: Slowest, but the safest. Plan ahead; it can take a day or longer.
Food stays safe the whole time.
Seal the food in a leak-proof bag and cover it with cold tap water. Change the water every 30 minutes.
Cook it before you refreeze it.
Cook it right away; parts of it may have started to cook.
table.note: Don’t thaw meat, poultry or seafood on the counter.

rows: Egg, chicken, tuna or macaroni salad
table.note: From FoodSafety.gov’s cold storage chart. Freezer times are for best quality; food kept frozen at 0°F stays safe. The free FoodKeeper app from USDA lists more than 650 foods.

p: Reheat leftovers to **165°F**, and bring soups, sauces and gravies to a rolling boil.

sections.h: Using and checking a food thermometer
list: Put the tip in the thickest part of the food, away from bone, fat and gristle. Check in two spots.
Wash the probe with hot, soapy water after each use.

To check a dial thermometer, stir a glass of crushed ice and water, wait a minute, and hold the stem in the middle without touching the glass. It should read 32°F. Many dials have a nut under the face to adjust.
Most digital thermometers can’t be adjusted; replace one that reads wrong in ice water.
